intro:
You settle a security baseline from security policies, design reviews, a team wiki, standup notes and email threads.

Initial specification:
- [e001] Precedence rule: when sources disagree, the order of authority is infosec-policy > design-review > team-wiki > standup > email-thread. Inside one source, the higher version wins.
- [e002] According to design-review DR-1 version 1, the minimum TLS version is `tls-v11`.
- [e003] According to design-review DR-1 version 1, the hash function is `sha3-512`.
- [e004] According to design-review DR-1 version 1, the session lifetime in minutes is `60`.
- [e005] According to design-review DR-1 version 1, the default log level is `level-error`.
- [e006] The design-review document DR-1 (version 1) states that the request tracing mode is `ON`.
- [e007] The design-review document DR-1 (version 1) states that the upload quota per hour is `250`.
- [e008] According to design-review DR-1 version 1, the key wrap algorithm is `kw-aes256`.
- [e009] The team-wiki document WIKI-115 (version 1) states that the maximum open files is `16384`.

Sources, from highest to lowest authority: infosec-policy, design-review, team-wiki, standup, email-thread. When two sources disagree, the higher one decides.
Inside one source, a higher version number overrides a lower one. A withdrawn document no longer counts at all.
Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.
